jobs.description: Amazon Customer Service supports customers around the world through one of the world’s largest and most diverse customer service workforces. As AI fundamentally changes how customer service work is performed, it also creates an opportunity to reinvent how associates learn, develop their capabilities, receive coaching, and continuously improve. The Associate Development team is building the next generation of learning, coaching and performance experiences for Amazon Customer Service Associates. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build these systems from the ground up. This is a highly greenfield opportunity. Rather than digitizing traditional training and coaching processes, we are rethinking how associate development should work in an AI-native world. What does an associate need to learn before doing a job? What can they learn through experience? What should AI provide in the flow of work? How can we understand an associate’s evolving capabilities and use that understanding to personalize development? How can generative AI help provide timely, relevant and effective coaching at the scale of a global workforce? Imagine systems that continuously learn from an associate’s experience and outcomes, identify where they would benefit from development, and deliver personalized learning or AI-powered coaching. The outcomes of those interventions can then become new evidence about the associate, creating a closed loop that gets smarter over time. As an SDE on this team, you will help define and build the technical foundations that make this possible. You will work on problems spanning generative AI, personalization, intelligent recommendations, learning and coaching systems, experimentation, data and distributed systems. You will have the opportunity to influence architecture at an early stage rather than inherit a predetermined technical solution. You will partner closely with Product, Science, UX and engineering teams across Amazon to turn ambiguous customer problems into scalable technical solutions. The systems you build have the potential to shape how Customer Service Associates around the world develop and succeed at work. This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys zero-to-one problems, emerging AI technologies, large-scale systems and building products with direct human impact. Key job responsibilities - Design and build scalable services and experiences that power personalized learning, coaching and associate development across Amazon Customer Service. - Build AI-powered coaching capabilities, including applications of generative AI that can understand context, generate relevant guidance and adapt experiences to individual associate needs. - Develop systems that connect signals about associate capability and performance with the right development intervention at the right time. - Help create closed-loop systems that measure the outcomes of learning and coaching interventions and use that evidence to continuously improve future recommendations. - Work with Product and Science partners to translate emerging models and experimentation into reliable production systems. - Make foundational architectural decisions for a greenfield product space while determining where existing Amazon capabilities can be reused or evolved. - Design APIs, data models and integration patterns that allow Associate Development capabilities to interact with associate context, workflow and other Customer Service systems. - Build mechanisms for experimentation, measurement and observability so we can understand whether the experiences we create actually improve associate and customer outcomes. - Deliver secure, reliable and globally scalable systems while maintaining a high bar for operational excellence. A day in the life You might start the day working with a scientist on how an AI coaching experience can use an associate’s recent performance context to generate more useful coaching. Later, you could whiteboard an architecture for measuring whether that coaching actually changed future performance, review an API contract with another CS platform team, and prototype a new generative-AI capability. Because the space is early, you won’t simply be executing against a fully specified roadmap. You will help answer fundamental technical questions, prototype alternatives, make architecture decisions, and turn successful experiments into production systems capable of serving associates globally. About the team The Associate Experience (AE) team is building the future of work for Amazon Customer Service Associates. Our vision is to create a trusted Customer Service experience by enabling associates to succeed as the role evolves toward complex and non-deterministic problem solving. Within AE, the Associate Development team is reinventing how associates learn, develop and improve, moving beyond one-size-fits-all training and coaching towards, personalized development powered by AI. Engineers joining the team will shape foundational architecture, drive technology choices, and build AI-powered products from the ground up for one of the world's largest customer service workforces.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Infrastructure organization builds and operates the distributed systems that train, serve, and secure our AI models. That includes data pipelines, some of the largest Kubernetes clusters in the world, and the databases, observability, and developer tooling that every other team at Anthropic depends on.
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Infrastructure team, you'll scope and lead complex, multi-month infrastructure projects, make the architectural decisions other engineers build on, and work with research and product teams to build systems that keep pace as their needs change.
Team placement happens after the interview process, based on your interests and experience alongside organizational needs. This helps us match you with the team where you'll have the most impact.
Key responsibilities
Independently scope and lead complex, multi-month infrastructure projects, from an ambiguous starting point through to a production system
Make architectural decisions that shape the foundation other engineers and teams build on
Drive alignment on technical direction across teams, working through ambiguous problem spaces
Partner with research and product teams to understand their infrastructure and compute needs, and turn them into technical designs
Own the reliability, scalability, and security of the systems you build as usage and complexity grow
Set technical strategy and standards for your team's infrastructure
Build and improve operational processes such as incident response, postmortems, and on-call rotations, so the team learns from every incident
Mentor other engineers and help raise the technical bar for the team
Minimum qualifications
Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or infrastructure in production
A history of independently scoping and delivering complex, ambiguous, multi-month technical projects
Experience making architectural decisions that other engineers and teams build on
Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in at least one programming language (for example, Python, Rust, Go, or Java)
Experience with modern cloud infrastructure, including Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code, on AWS and/or GCP
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience driving alignment across teams or stakeholders
Preferred qualifications
10+ years of software engineering experience, not including internships
Experience with machine learning infrastructure such as GPUs, TPUs, or Trainium, and associated networking like NCCL
Low-level systems experience, such as Linux kernel tuning or eBPF
Background in security or privacy engineering best practices
Prior experience as a technical lead or mentor for other engineers

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
The world's engineers want to get the most out of Claude. At Anthropic, technical instruction already happens everywhere: our Applied AI and Forward Deployed Engineering teams teach customers and partners, and engineers across the company help others learn to build with Claude. Today that instruction is a shared responsibility, delivered alongside people's primary roles. As demand grows, we need to turn that distributed expertise into a dedicated technical instruction function.
You will build that function.
You will be the first person at Anthropic whose full-time job is technical instruction. You'll spend your first year primarily in the classroom teaching engineers, architects, and other technical practitioners. You'll also build the people, standards, and systems that let Anthropic's technical instruction scale far beyond the people we directly employ.
This is a player-coach role. From day one you manage a small bench of instructors. You set the bar for what "ready to teach" means, decide who is cleared to teach a given module in Anthropic's technical programs, and assess facilitators from our training partners against that bar.
You're an engineer who teaches and a teacher who has led other teachers. You can build an agent live in front of a skeptical engineer, diagnose what isn't working in a technical lab, and make the material better. You can also watch an experienced instructor teach, tell them their session isn't ready yet, and coach them to get there.
You will report to the Head of Technical Enablement. The role is based in San Francisco with some travel expected.
Key responsibilities
Lead from the front.
Teach hands-on sessions to new Applied AI engineers, our field teams, and partner cohorts, in rooms from 12-person labs to 100-person training days.
Build the instructor bench.
Hire and develop instructors and curriculum developers. Decide contract renewals, and recommend conversions to full-time, against criteria you define.
Set the quality bar.
Own the observation rubric, dry-run protocol, and cleared-to-teach process for every instructor-led technical session.
Scale through train-the-trainer.
Set the bar the Lead Technical Instructor's train-the-trainer program teaches to, for internal experts, contract instructors, and partner facilitators.
Turn expertise into instruction.
Turn internal experts' content into sessions and labs that work in a live room.
Enable programs without owning them.
Staff other teams' programs with cleared instructors, and own the quality of instruction inside them.
Measure and improve.
Report learner pass rates per instructor each month, and act on them.
Minimum qualifications
8+ years of relevant professional experience
across software engineering, solutions engineering, developer advocacy, technical education, or related technical roles.
4+ years of hands-on technical instruction.
You have taught engineers live and hands-on, across audience sizes.
Production engineering.
You have written and shipped production software and engage credibly with experienced engineers on architecture and debugging.
Recent hands-on AI development.
In your last three years of work, you have built or debugged applications with LLM APIs, agent frameworks, tool use, MCP, or similar.
People leadership.
You have managed instructors, trainers, developer advocates, or solutions engineers, including hiring and performance management, and kept teaching.
Instructor development.
You have designed or run a train-the-trainer program, instructor certification, or observation framework.
San Francisco location.
You are based in San Francisco or willing to relocate with our relocation support, can be in the office every day a program runs, 3 days in a normal week, and can travel 25 to 30 percent.
Preferred qualifications
A portfolio of sessions you taught and a rubric or certification you designed, shared only if you have the right.
Experience building an instruction or developer-education function from scratch.
Experience managing a contractor instructor bench, or clearing instructors across regions from recordings or trained observers.
Daily use of Claude Code or a comparable agentic coding tool, or building on Claude through Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry.
Deep enthusiasm for AI and real care about building it responsibly.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Experience in power plants, nuclear power plants, data centers, or facilities like SpaceXAI — current or prior — spanning power, compute, cooling, or related plant systems.

Cross-team facilitation and systems engineering depth across software and facility boundaries.

MTTD / MTTR trend for SEV-class events
% of SEVs with a blameless postmortem and closed action items
Alert actionable ratio

jobs.description: We are looking for a Solutions Architect to join the AWS Bedrock Customer Success Engineering Escalations and Engagements Team (CSET-ENE). This is a customer-facing role, and our engagements often occur at the most difficult points in a customer's journey with our services. As a Solutions Architect on the team you will own technical investigations end to end for the engagements assigned to you: understanding what the customer experienced, determining root cause, explaining service behavior, and helping rebuild customer confidence after an event. The business objective and the priority will usually be clear — "this customer cannot get the throughput they provisioned," "these inference requests are failing and we don't know why." The technical solution design and the path to the answer will not be. You figure that out, and you know when a problem has grown complex enough that a Senior or Principal SA should be pulled in. You will communicate clearly, concisely, accurately, and in a timely manner. You will write Root Cause Analyses and customer messaging to a publishable bar, run technical meetings with customers and with internal teams, and consult on current and planned customer architectures. Because CSET engages closely with customers during vulnerable periods in their use of our services, this role requires emotional intelligence and judgment about how much detail an audience needs. You will also build. On this team, an SA's leverage is expressed in the internal software they write — investigation tooling, knowledge pipelines, automation that turns one engineer's expertise into the team's baseline. You own components and tools end to end, and you contribute into the platforms senior members of the team own. This is a first-class part of the job, not a side activity. Key job responsibilities **Customer engagements & escalations** - Own technical investigations for assigned escalations and engagements: gather evidence, form and test a hypothesis, and drive to a defensible root cause rather than a plausible story. - Reproduce customer issues to validate root cause and mitigation. - Take a well-formed problem statement to the service team — with the data that supports it — and follow it through to a fix or a documented decision. - Support high-stakes engagements led by senior members of the team, and escalate proactively when risk, ambiguity, or customer sentiment exceeds your level. - Resolve the root cause of difficult problems, whether the problem is the customer's or ours. **Architecture & enablement** - Advise customers on current and planned architectures, best practices, and work-arounds to known issues, applying the trade-off reasoning behind each recommendation rather than reciting guidance. - Reduce customer cases by owning the development, delivery, review, and maintenance of technical content: knowledge articles, best-practice guides, runbooks, demos, and documentation corrections. - Feed every engagement back into the team's knowledge base so the next investigator does not start from zero. **Communication** - Author RCAs and customer wording that stand up to review with minimal rework, and apply the team's approved wording and terminology standards. - Run effective meetings internally and with customers, express a clear technical opinion, and build agreement on a way forward. - Convey difficult technical topics — verbally, in writing, and by diagram — to both technical and non-technical audiences. - Contribute to team narratives and post-event reviews. **Building & mechanisms** - Design, write, ship, and operate internal tooling in the team's languages (primarily Python; Rust and TypeScript in the Bedrock codebases we own). - Build for reuse: installable, documented, and tested, so the tool runs without you in the room. - Apply secure-by-default practices without being asked — provider-based credentials rather than hardcoded ones, least-privilege access, and careful handling of customer data. - Codify what you learn: investigation patterns, lessons, and validators the whole team and our agents run. - Improve team process efficiency, and contribute to cross-team process improvements. **Team** - Participate in interviews and help recruit for the team. - Mentor newer teammates and share what you learn from engagements.
